property_summary: If an address is set as an approved logger via setApprovedLogger(addr,true), then approvedToLog(addr) returns true.
Only addresses explicitly approved via setApprovedLogger can cause logCreated to emit (i.e., logCreated returns true) — an unapproved address cannot log.

For every address input, the reference contract's approvedToLog(address) returns the mapping value approvedLoggers[address] (so it can be true for some addresses), whereas the mutant always returns false for all addresses, violating that there exists an address for which approvedToLog returns true when approvedLoggers[address] is set to true.

For any address a, if the owner enables a as an approved logger via setApprovedLogger(a, true), then approvedToLog(a) returns true; the mutant that always returns false violates this for those enabled addresses.
For any address a, if the contract owner enables a via setApprovedLogger(a, true), then approvedToLog(a) must return true; the mutant that always returns false violates this for enabled addresses.

For any address caller, if the contract owner disables that caller via setApprovedLogger(caller, false) then approvedToLog(caller) returns false (reference satisfies for all inputs); the mutant that always returns false still satisfies this, so instead use the complementary universal rule: for any address caller, after the owner enables the caller via setApprovedLogger(caller, true), approvedToLog(caller) returns true — the mutant breaks this for enabled addresses.

For every address a, if the contract owner enables a via setApprovedLogger(a, true) then approvedToLog(a) returns true; the mutant that always returns false violates this because it never returns true for any enabled address.

For any input address A, calling approvedToLog(A) returns approvedLoggers[A] (i.e., it depends only on the provided _caller); the mutant instead depends on tx.origin so for some fuzzed address and call context the return differs.

For every address caller the reference's approvedToLog(caller) returns the mapping entry approvedLoggers[caller] (i.e., it depends only on the provided argument); the mutant breaks this by instead returning approvedLoggers[tx.origin], so when a contract (not an EOA) calls approvedToLog(someAddress) the reference can return based on that argument but the mutant will base the answer on tx.origin and thus differ for some inputs.

For any (fuzzed) target address X and any caller (which may be a contract), the reference contract's approvedToLog(X) returns approvedLoggers[X] (i.e. depends only on the argument); the mutant instead reads approvedLoggers[tx.origin], so when a contract calls approvedToLog(X) with tx.origin != X the mutant can return a different value and thus violate this rule.

For every address x and any caller context, the reference contract's approvedToLog(x) always returns the mapping entry approvedLoggers[x] (i.e., depends only on the provided argument); the mutant instead returns approvedLoggers[tx.origin], so when a contract (caller) invokes approvedToLog(x) with tx.origin != x the mutant can return a different value and thus violate this property.

For any address caller, when a contract C.approvedToLog is invoked via a contract caller (so tx.origin != that contract's address), the reference returns approvedLoggers[arg] (depends only on the argument) while the mutant instead returns approvedLoggers[tx.origin]; thus if tx.origin and the passed argument differ and their approvedLoggers entries differ the mutant's return will differ — the rule: for any calleeArg and any callerContract the return equals approvedLoggers[calleeArg]; the bug breaks this when tx.origin != calleeArg and approvedLoggers[tx.origin] != approvedLoggers[calleeArg].

For every address input, approvedToLog(address) returns true iff approvedLoggers[address] is true (i.e., it returns the mapping entry value directly); the mutant inverts the comparison so some addresses that are true become false (or vice versa), causing the property to fail for those inputs.

For every address x, approvedToLog(x) returns the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[x]; the mutant that compares to false flips the result when the stored value is true, so there exists an address x with approvedLoggers[x]==true for which the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For every address a, approvedToLog(a) returns the actual stored mapping value approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant flips the boolean comparison so when an address has been set to true the mutant will return false, violating this rule.

For any address a, calling approvedToLog(a) must return the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant that compares to false flips the returned boolean for addresses whose mapping entry is true, so there exists an address a with approvedLoggers[a]==true where the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For every address a, after the owner enables it via setApprovedLogger(a, true), approvedToLog(a) must return true; the mutant's faulty comparison returns false for such enabled addresses, so the property is violated for any address the fuzzer picks and the owner enables.
Only the contract owner can set approvedLoggers (setApprovedLogger succeeds only when called by the owner).

property_summary: Calls to setApprovedLogger(msg.sender, status) made from this contract revert (i.e. are not allowed) for all inputs when msg.sender is not the contract owner of C.
Calls to setApprovedLogger sent from this test contract revert iff the test contract's address is not equal to C's owner (so when this contract is the owner the call does not revert).
Only the owner address is allowed to successfully call setApprovedLogger when invoked from this test contract: calls from this contract revert exactly when this contract is not C's owner.
Calls to setApprovedLogger(msg.sender, status) from this test contract revert whenever this test contract is not the recorded owner of C, and succeed whenever it is the owner.

For every address a, only the contract owner can call functions guarded by onlyOwner (setting approvedLoggers) — the mutant inverts the check so some non-owner can be prevented/allowed incorrectly, causing approvedLoggers[a] to differ for some fuzzed owner/non-owner pair and logger address.

In the correct contract, only the designated contract owner can change approvedLoggers via setApprovedLogger, so for any addresses owner and logger, if the owner calls setApprovedLogger(logger, status) then c.approvedLoggers(logger) equals status afterwards; the mutant inverts the onlyOwner check and thus there exist owner/logger inputs where invoking setApprovedLogger from the intended owner does not set approvedLoggers(logger) (or sets it incorrectly).

For any caller 'actor' and target 'logger', when the designated contract owner (the deployer) calls setApprovedLogger(logger, status) the public getter approvedLoggers(logger) equals status afterwards; the mutant inverts onlyOwner so there exist inputs where this no longer holds (the owner call is rejected and the mapping is not updated).

For every addresses caller (who performs the setApprovedLogger call) and logger and boolean status, if the caller is the contract owner then setApprovedLogger(caller's tx sender, logger, status) will successfully set approvedLoggers(logger) to status; the mutant inverts the owner check so there exist inputs where the true owner cannot set the mapping and the getter differs.

For every address logger and boolean status, if a non-owner caller invokes setApprovedLogger(logger, status) the call must NOT change approvedLoggers(logger) (only owner can change it); the mutant inverts the owner check so there exist fuzzed (caller,logger,status) where a non-owner call wrongly changes the mapping.

For every address a and boolean s, calling setApprovedLogger(a, s) by the contract owner sets approvedLoggers(a) equal to s; the mutant inverts the stored value so for some inputs approvedLoggers(a) != s.

For any address logger and boolean status set by the contract owner, after calling setApprovedLogger(logger, status) the stored approvedLoggers(logger) equals status; the mutant negates status when storing, so for some (owner,logger,status) the mutant yields approvedLoggers(logger) != status.

For any owner caller and target logger address, toggling the logger status twice with the SAME boolean value leaves the approvedLoggers entry unchanged in the reference (idempotent for repeated identical sets), but the mutant (which stores !_status) will flip the stored value on each call and thus can change the final stored value after two identical calls.
